traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-17): simple leaves, no lobing; Lucid key (read 2026-10-17): none.

traits.leaf_margin.note: DELTA, Nyctaginaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire; Lucid key (read 2026-10-17): margins entire.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Nyctaginaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves usually opposite, pair members often unequal.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Nyctaginaceae: leaves usually opposite, sometimes alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes monoecious or polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary, in cymes, in panicles, in spikes or in umbels; flowers actinomorphic; perianth tepals; fruit achene or nut; stamens (1-) 5 (-30); carpels 1. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.perianth.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add absent (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 378: tepals; a single petaloid calyx, corolla absent.

traits.sexual_system.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add dioecious (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 378: hermaphrodite or dioecious.

traits.bract_form.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 187, family Nyctaginaceae: bract form large involucral bracts, often petaloid, enclosing the flowers, often; read as {"petaloid": "often"}.
